title: Normalized internal principal-cone augmentation at one level
statement: Let $l$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_l$ finite, $X$ any scheme, and $d$ an endomorphism of the regular continuous integral coefficient module whose value on every continuous function $f$ at every point is $\pi_E f$. For an unbounded categorically K-flat complex $P$ of internal modules on $X$ and every $n\geq0$, there is a quasi-isomorphism $a:\operatorname{Cone}(\mu_P^{n+1})\to P\otimes B_{n+1}$, where $\mu_P=\operatorname{scalarOnComplex}(d,P)$ and the target is the specified termwise reduction. In degree $q$ it is exactly the unshifted cone projection followed by $\operatorname{levelUnit}(P,n)$; its shifted cone component is zero. The coefficient objects, scalar action and level unit are those of [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution] and [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], and the cone convention is [def-pur-principal-cone-tower].

source.place: Lemma lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism, and algebraization.tex lemma-derived-completion-koszul (Tag 0A0E); regular singleton quotient resolution.

proof.text: The pointwise hypothesis identifies d with the concrete uniformizerEnd by extensionality. Pull back its exact positive-power coefficient sequence, and conjugate its first two objects by regularPullbackIso. The resulting maps are r on the monoidal unit and exactly finiteUnit. Conjugation, functoriality and unitEndAction preserve powers, identifying the scalar on P with the required power.

For any scalar r and quotient p of the monoidal unit in a braided closed Grothendieck abelian category with functorial flat resolutions, define rho termwise by the right unitor inverse followed by tensor with p. Scalar linearity gives r followed by rho equal to zero. Define a to be mappingCone.descShortComplex for this short complex. Its degreewise formula has zero shifted component. For complexes with flat terms, tensor the coefficient short exact sequence in each degree and use right unitors to identify it with the short complex of complexes. The canonical cone augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism by Mathlib mappingCone.quasiIso_descShortComplex.

Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution K to P. The diagonal scalar-cone map is a quasi-isomorphism by the morphism of distinguished cone triangles. TensorRight(B) preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes, by acyclic_tensorRight_of_kFlat and PreservesKFlatQuasiIso.mk'. Naturality of rho gives a morphism of the short complexes, and mappingCone.map_descShortComplex gives a commuting augmentation square. Three maps are quasi-isomorphisms, so the fourth is. Rewrite the cone scalar equality and use the specified finiteUnit for the conclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem internal_principal_cone_level_augmentation
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (d : End (Mod.regular (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E)))
    (hd : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}ᵒᵖ) (f : (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E).obj.obj S)
      (s : S.unop), ((d.hom.hom.app S) f).down s =
        Padic.coefficientExtensionUniformizer l E * f.down s)
    (P : CochainComplex (Modules l E X) ℤ)
    (hP : (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (Modules l E X) (.up ℤ)).kFlat P)
    (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ a : CochainComplex.PrincipalCone.level
        (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X d P) n ⟶ (level l E X n).obj P,
      QuasiIso a ∧ ∀ q : ℤ, a.f q =
        (CochainComplex.mappingCone.snd
          (End.of (DerivedNakayama.scalarOnComplex l E X d P) ^ (n + 1))).v q q (add_zero q) ≫
            (levelUnit l E X P n).f q
